newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Specialist funds beat the index in Asia - survey.
newsitem.headline: Specialist funds beat the index in Asia - survey.

text.p: Specialist portfolios investing in Asian markets excluding Japan outperformed the comparable investment index in 1996, according to performance measurement consultancy WM Company.

The WM Asian ex Japan Investment Funds Universe, which includes results for 17 investment portfolios worth a total of US$2.3 billion, shows that the funds produced an average return of 13.9 percent in 1996.

By contrast, the Morgan Stanley Capital International All Countries Far East Free Ex Japan (MSCI) index return was just 11.1 percent. The MSCI index represents the stocks available in the region to foreign investors.
Hong Kong produced the best returns at an average gain of 42.2 percent, but these varied considerably among fund managers, with gains between 23.7 and 51.9 percent recorded.
While the average fund held 39 percent of its assets in Hong Kong, the region's largest market, the proportion held by individual funds varied between 17 percent and 52 percent.

"Our analysis shows there is often a significant difference in strategy between the managers but the funds generally got Hong Kong right and that is a key reason for their good overall performance," said Colin Kay, a director at WM Company.
